verdict.reasons: The core commercial product is clearly present and correctly identified as a roll of AFP drip tape. The 'Drip Irrigation Tape' label and associated logo match the specified guidelines, and the package identity is visually consistent with the reference. However, the image fails the 'technical_evidence_match' and 'irrigation_geometry_plausible' requirements because it depicts the packaging (the cylindrical carton) sitting on the ground as an independent object, rather than showing the actual tape laid out on a continuous irrigation header and connected to a take-off fitting. The instruction explicitly requires identifying 'commercial product rolls or packages, not supporting infrastructure,' but this candidate is not using the product as a roll or package of the actual tape in an active system; instead, it uses the packaging sleeve in a way that misrepresents the installation. The gauge shown is not part of a continuous header and does not reflect a valid drip-tape installation scene as described. These issues represent core defects that prevent the image from being a useful, technically accurate illustration of drip-tape pressure management.

focused_physical_review.reason: The white drip tape coil rests with packed soil directly abutting its base and left side, meaning no broad uninterrupted soil gap surrounds the complete footprint. No irrigation line is visible at or emerging from the base of the AFP carton; the only visible line is installed in the adjacent gauge fixture. There is no distinct loose uninstalled coil or roll outside the required package, though a short white plastic strip/ribbon tail protrudes from the left side near the base, constituting a physical package defect.

acceptance_warnings: Independent physical condition not met: clear_soil_gap
Independent physical condition not met: package_has_protruding_strip
